questions.q: Benzaldehyde is refluxed with a small amount of KCN in aqueous ethanol. The product is:
questions.explain: Alcoholic KCN catalyses the benzoin condensation, joining the two former carbonyl carbons to give an α-hydroxy ketone. Concentrated NaOH would give the Cannizzaro products, and benzil needs a later oxidation.

questions.q: The role of cyanide in the benzoin condensation is that of a:
options: Reducing agent that converts one aldehyde into an alcohol
Catalyst that reverses the polarity (umpolung) of the carbonyl carbon and is regenerated
Reagent that is incorporated as a nitrile group in the product
Base that removes an α-hydrogen to form an enolate
questions.explain: CN⁻ adds to the aldehyde, makes the former carbonyl C–H acidic so that carbon becomes a nucleophilic carbanion, and is expelled at the end. Benzaldehyde has no α-hydrogen, so no enolate is involved.

questions.q: Why does ethanal not give a benzoin-type product with alcoholic KCN?
options: Ethanal does not react with CN⁻ at all
Cyanide is too weak a nucleophile for aliphatic aldehydes
The acyloin formed from ethanal is immediately oxidised
The carbanion after cyanide addition lacks stabilisation by a benzene ring, and in base ethanal mostly undergoes aldol reactions
questions.explain: In benzaldehyde the carbanion is stabilised by both –CN and the phenyl ring. Aliphatic aldehydes lack the ring, so they need thiazolium (thiamine-type) catalysts instead.

questions.q: Benzaldehyde is converted into X with alcoholic KCN; X is oxidised by nitric acid to Y; Y is heated with KOH and then acidified to give Z. Z is:
questions.explain: X is benzoin, Y is the 1,2-diketone benzil, and the benzilic acid rearrangement of benzil gives Z, (C₆H₅)₂C(OH)COOH. This benzoin → benzil → benzilic acid sequence is a classic three-step chain.
